e2f9503e43f3bb1947bbbe9bf4729f62f8434e1d.summary: Symantec reports that Carderbee, a previously unknown APT group, carried out a supply chain attack using the legitimate Cobra DocGuard software to deploy the Korplug (PlugX) backdoor. Most victims are in Hong Kong, and the attackers used malware signed with a Microsoft certificate. About 100 computers showed malicious activity while the software was installed on around 2,000. Symantec could not link the activity to a known group. ESET earlier attributed a 2022 compromise of a Hong Kong gambling company, using the same software, to Budworm.

e28eb63dbc097b3e208b713fdbbea41bcdbd4022.summary: Recorded Future News reports that Sun Pharmaceuticals, an Indian pharmaceutical company, confirmed a ransomware attack in regulatory filings. Company data and personal data were stolen, and business operations were affected. The company did not name the group that claimed the attack. The Black Cat/AlphV ransomware group listed the company on its leak site on March 24. The company warned of lower revenue, higher cyber insurance costs and possible litigation.

e2b54bb7ea7cc5df374fc2d205488fd4391af8c3.summary: News report on MoneyTaker, a cybercriminal group believed to be operating from Russian-speaking territories. Group-IB, a Russian security firm, first described it and named it after one of its hacking utilities. Group-IB says the group began in 2016 and hit at least 20 banks and financial companies, mainly targeting inter-bank money transfer and card processing systems. Reported tools include the MoneyTaker framework, ScanPOS, Citadel and Kronos. Group-IB could not find the initial infection vector.
